title: Semantic Zoom
description: Changes what is shown — not just size — as users zoom: boxes become modules become code. Each level has its own representation; transitions are the design. It matches how architects think.

demo.title: Demo — Semantic Zoom

title: Level-of-Detail Rendering
description: Renders detail proportional to zoom: far means boxes, near means text. LOD keeps massive diagrams interactive; detail appears exactly when readable. It is how maps work, applied to code.

demo.title: Demo — Level-of-Detail Rendering

title: C4 Model Navigation
description: Navigates architecture through C4's four levels: context, containers, components, code. Each level answers different questions; zooming moves between them. It structures architectural thinking.

demo.title: Demo — C4 Model Navigation

title: Diagram Tile Pyramids
description: Serves huge diagrams as tile pyramids like web maps: pre-rendered at each zoom, fetched on demand. Gigapixel architecture diagrams become browsable; only visible tiles load. It scales infinitely.

demo.title: Demo — Diagram Tile Pyramids

title: Vector Tile Diagrams
description: Streams diagrams as vector tiles for crisp zoom at any level. Vectors stay sharp; styling adapts per zoom. It is the modern map stack applied to architecture.

demo.title: Demo — Vector Tile Diagrams

title: Progressive Disclosure
description: Reveals complexity progressively: overview first, details on demand. Users are never overwhelmed; curiosity drives the drill-down. It respects cognitive limits.

demo.title: Demo — Progressive Disclosure

title: Zoom-to-Code
description: Zooms from architecture diagrams directly into the source file and line. The diagram and code are one navigable space; there is no context switch. It unifies the abstract and concrete.

demo.title: Demo — Zoom-to-Code

title: Minimap Overlays
description: Shows a minimap overview with the viewport rectangle during deep zooms. Users never get lost; the minimap is the compass. Editors and games proved the pattern.

demo.title: Demo — Minimap Overlays

title: GPU-Accelerated Canvas
description: Renders diagrams on the GPU for smooth zoom of massive graphs. Canvas and WebGL batch thousands of nodes; the CPU stays free. Performance enables exploration.

demo.title: Demo — GPU-Accelerated Canvas

title: Infinite Canvas
description: Lays architecture on an infinite canvas with pan and zoom as the navigation. No pages, no hierarchy constraints; space is the organizer. Whiteboard tools made it familiar.

demo.title: Demo — Infinite Canvas

title: Layer Culling
description: Culls off-screen and irrelevant layers during zoom for performance. Only visible content renders; the rest waits. It keeps frame rates high at any scale.

demo.title: Demo — Layer Culling

title: Zoom-Level Prefetching
description: Prefetches adjacent zoom levels so zooming never waits on the network. The current level plus neighbors stay cached; zoom feels instant. It hides latency with prediction.

demo.title: Demo — Zoom-Level Prefetching

title: Gesture Zoom Handling
description: Handles pinch and wheel zoom with the right physics: momentum, bounds, snapping. The feel of zoom decides whether the tool delights or frustrates. Native gestures set expectations.

demo.title: Demo — Gesture Zoom Handling

title: Zoom State Persistence
description: Persists zoom position and level across sessions via shareable URLs. A link opens exactly the view the sender saw; collaboration needs it. State is part of the document.

demo.title: Demo — Zoom State Persistence

title: Zoom Usability Studies
description: Studies whether zoomable architecture actually helps with task-based evaluations. Navigation time, lostness, and insight versus static diagrams; evidence guides design. It keeps the field honest.

demo.title: Demo — Zoom Usability Studies
